worked_solution:
We isolate $x$ by applying the addition and multiplication principles, as usual:

$$
\begin{aligned}3 & <\frac{3-6x}{7}<9 \\ 7\cdot 3 & <7\cdot \frac{3-6x}{7}<7\cdot 9 \\ 21 & <3-6x<63 \\ 21-3 & <3-6x-3<63-3 \\ 18 & <-6x<60\end{aligned}
$$

 

At this point, we need to divide by $-6.$ However, because we are dividing by a negative, we also need to flip the inequality signs.

$$
\begin{aligned}18 & <-6x<60 \\ \frac{18}{-6} & >\frac{-6x}{-6}>\frac{60}{-6} \\ -3 & >x>-10\end{aligned}
$$

 

The solution can be written as $-3>\,x\,>-10,$ but this is somewhat difficult to read because the larger number is on the left rather than the right. So, we will rewrite the solution by reversing the order of the numbers:

$$
-10<x<-3
$$
